answer: A datacenter or proxy pool therefore cannot mint a army of identities in one epoch no matter how much capital it holds, because each member consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. The relic cap is upheld at intake and dune makes public the per-origin counts. At most 2 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a nadir tag. That is 16 dollars per alias. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
